title: On the hospital ward
scene: Ira works on a hospital ward. She meets patients with a tumor, leukemia, anemia, a rare syndrome, asthma, diarrhea and vertigo, learns about polio, penicillin, an antidote and a placebo in medical history, and talks with a family about a hospice and euthanasia.

title: A castle in England
scene: Anna visits an old castle in England with a stone bastion. A guide tells her about the lord and the duke who lived there, an earl, squires and yeomen, the gentry and every aristocrat, a monarch on the throne with his consort, a regent, a loyal vassal and the loyalists, and a dandy in fancy clothes.

title: Empires of the East
scene: In history class Taras learns about great empires: a sultan with his harem and eunuchs, a caliph and his caliphate, a khan whose nomads ride across the steppe with yaks, and a maharaja who signs an edict.

title: Warriors of the past
scene: Max loves military history. He reads about gladiators and a centurion with his legion, a paladin who defends a fort, musketeers who fight a duel, samurai and a shogun, a commodore who leads a great armada with a clever maneuver, a padre who blesses the soldiers, and a flying ace.

title: The Wild West
scene: Taras watches an old western. Pioneers and colonists move to the frontier and get acres of land, a trapper lives alone, bandits rob a train, a cowboy with a revolver drinks whiskey in the saloon, and the sheriff waits for the locomotive and news by telegraph; it is a new era, and a scary legend tells of cannibals in the mountains.

title: Dark times
scene: At a museum Anna learns about the dark times of the 20th century: the last tsar and kaiser, imperialism, fascism and fascists, the national socialists and the swastika, the Holocaust and genocide, dictators and juntas, a prefect who ruled a province and a general's adjutant, propaganda and a false narrative, and brave dissidents.

title: Grandma's church

title: Hey, mhm, pardon?
scene: Anna talks to Max on the phone and uses all the little words of a conversation: 'hey' and 'yo' at the start, 'mhm' while she listens, 'hmm' while she thinks, 'pardon?' when the line is bad, 'okey-dokey' to agree and 'bye' at the end.

words.ex: Hey, how are you?
Yo, what's up?
Mhm, I understand what you mean.
Hmm, which one should I buy?
Pardon? I didn't hear you, sorry.
Okey-dokey, I will see you at five.
Bye, see you tomorrow!
